topic: Slope and Area Interpretation of Motion Graphs
title: Slope and Area of Graphs Explained Simply | PUC Physics Class 11
description:
Aarav's bicycle meter shows only his speed, never his distance. Yet he can find the distance from the speed graph alone. In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Physics (NCERT Chapter 2, Motion in a Straight Line) we learn the two tools that read every motion graph: slope and area.

You will watch Aarav's ride on a live simulation with a velocity-time graph that draws as he moves, a slow-motion replay of the braking with velocity and acceleration vectors, and the area under the graph growing exactly as his distance grows. We show step by step why the slope of an x-t graph is velocity, the slope of a v-t graph is acceleration, the area under a v-t graph is displacement and the area under an a-t graph is the change in velocity, and why thin strips make the area add up to the distance. Then a worked example, the exam trap about area below the time axis, an original JEE Main / NEET pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, JEE Main and NEET students.

In this video:
0:00 A speed meter and a hidden distance
0:29 Two tools: slope and area
0:54 Aarav's ride: live v-t graph and slow-mo braking
1:30 Slope and area, step by step
2:18 Why area equals displacement: thin strips
2:45 Side by side + pause and think
3:45 Worked example: acceleration and displacement
4:21 Exam trap: area below the axis
4:45 Practice question (JEE Main / NEET pattern)
5:24 Recap and three questions to answer

Next episode: Relative Motion in One Dimension. Two buses move side by side at the same speed. Why does each look still to the other?
